Hi Stephanie,

We're kicking off our annual renewal conversation and wanted to flag a couple of constraints on our side before you prepare a formal proposal. Over the last 9 months our usage profile shifted: we saw a sustained spike in generation for a pilot that will end Q1 next year. That means our true long-term baseline is lower than the numbers on our current invoice.

We want to avoid a cliff increase at renewal if usage normalizes — looking for approaches that give predictable unit pricing but also protections (smoothing/true-up) so we don't get a surprise 40% bill increase if the pilot winds down.

Can we set up a call next week? In the meantime, if you can draft 2–3 renewal sizing options with safeguards (smoothing window, cap on % uplift, and true-up timing) that would be useful.

Thanks,
Erin Palmer

Team — forwarding Erin's note. HelioHealth is explicitly asking for renewal options that avoid a large step-up if the pilot drops off. Quick thoughts below; I'm attaching a workbook to work from. Please reply with redlines by EOD Wed so I can send a tidy proposal on Thursday.

Proposed structure (sketch):
- Option A: Baseline commit (conservative), small per-token discount, 60-day true-up window, one-time smoothing credit if usage drops >25% versus prior 3 months.
- Option B: Elastic band (commit range), per-token tiering with smoothing over a quarter, a 12% max renewal uplift cap year-over-year for the first renewal period.
- Add-on: Temporary pilot tranche (time-boxed) charged at a discounted overage rate with explicit sunset.

Operational asks: include a clear definition of "baseline" (rolling 90-day median), true-up cadence, and an SLA fallback if we need to migrate to a smaller model variant.

Attachments: Helio_Renewal_Workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Nice summary, Steph. A few adjustments I suggest before we share externally:

- Define the smoothing window explicitly as a 90-day rolling smoothing applied at the invoice level; preserves predictability without penalizing short pilots.
- Instead of a flat 12% uplift cap, propose a stepped protection: max 15% on the first renewal, 20% on subsequent renewals, subject to usage trend. Keeps us flexible but still gives Helio a boundary.
- Offer a "pilot tranche" discount with a clear sunset and automatic reclassification into baseline at the end date to avoid surprise credits.
- For legal: include a two-way true-up (if usage rises above commit, standard true-up; if usage falls >25% vs baseline, customer gets a one-time adjustment credit equal to the difference for the quarter).

I'll draft suggested language for the proposal doc. Marissa — can you sanity-check the financial impact model in the workbook and flag if any of these options break our margin thresholds? Ben — want your take on whether we can stretch the first-renewal uplift cap to 15% without underwriting risk.

Thanks,
Karthik

Option 1 (Conservative commit)
- Fixed baseline commit aligned to 6-month rolling median
- Per-token price: $0.0009 (hosted API gen)
- 60-day invoice true-up; one-time smoothing credit if usage falls more than 25% vs the prior quarter

Option 2 (Elastic band — recommended)
- Commit range (lower bound / upper bound) with tiered per-token pricing inside band
- Rolling 90-day smoothing window applied monthly
- First renewal uplift cap: 15% (year-over-year); subsequent renewals reviewed
- Pilot tranche (time-boxed) at 30% discounted overage; auto-sunset at pilot end

We can also add a short contract clause that defines baseline, true-up mechanics, and an emergency rollback path in case of unexpected production regressions.

1) Can you extend the smoothing/true-up window to 90 days instead of 60? That gives us more time to observe post-pilot normalization.
2) Can we tighten the first-renewal uplift cap to 15% and make the cap absolute for the first 12 months (i.e., no other ad-hoc uplifts in that term)?

Both items are manageable for us and would make the renewal acceptable to finance. If you agree, please send a redline and we can fast-track legal.
